data.what_it_does: Generates 128-bit identifiers combining a 48-bit timestamp and 80 random bits, canonically encoded as 26-character strings. It provides sortable IDs that replace traditional UUIDs when chronological ordering is required.
use_when: You need unique identifiers that are also sortable by creation time.
You prefer 26-character strings over traditional 36-character UUIDs.
avoid_when: You only need standard random UUIDs without timestamp sorting requirements.
strengths: Supports custom random sources and monotonic increments via UlidFactory
Cross-platform support including Dart-only web and mobile
weaknesses: Some older methods like toCanonical are deprecated in favor of toBase32
toString casing behavior is scheduled to change in a future major version

alternatives.name: uuid
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need standard RFC-compliant UUIDs instead of ULIDs.
